subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should trusted hook-agent callers be allowed to opt into resuming an existing stored session, and which authorization, session-key-prefix, agent, and delivery constraints define that boundary?
rationale: The implementation can preserve the existing default, but maintainer intent is required because opting into persistence changes which externally triggered requests may reach retained agent context.

options.title: Explicit persistent mode with existing gates
options.body: Keep `isolated` as the default and accept a narrowly documented persistent mode only after current-main review proves that hook authentication, allowed prefixes, and target scoping remain enforced.

options.title: Keep hooks permanently isolated
options.body: Reject session resumption for hook-agent requests and correct the documentation so stable hook session keys are not represented as multi-turn context.

recommendation.title: Explicit persistent mode with existing gates
recommendation.body: Keep `isolated` as the default and accept a narrowly documented persistent mode only after current-main review proves that hook authentication, allowed prefixes, and target scoping remain enforced.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review comment records the preferred explicit-mode direction and frames the outstanding security decision.
